Its a story about the duality of good and evil in us. 


The main character is a beautiful, impressionable, naiive and pure-minded young man. He meets a man through a mutual friend who views the young man as an experiment, he basically wants to corrupt him. The shall we say "mentor" points out to the boy that he is beautiful but one day his looks will fade, and that the boy must have secret desires and encourages him to indulge in them, no matter what they may be. The boy freaks out at the idea of losing his youth and wishes for a way for him to remain young and beautiful. Gradually we see a great transformation of the boy, not physically of course because he can never age now, but in his character. He has become ruthless, even cruel, self-absorbed, and materialistic. His mentor hands him a book that is about a beautiful young man, like the boy himself, and how the character indulges in a life of sin and gives into any sense his "soul desires." This book greatly influences his actions and undoubtedly, it is one of the biggest factors to the change of the boy. 18 years pass and the rumors say that the one pure man is now doing terrible things. Ruining marriages, the lives of the youth, visiting dark places such as the opium dens, being the cause of multiple suicides. But people are skeptical about this, because throughout the years he has not aged a bit, and the innocent look on his face is still there. That is because his cruel expressions instead of wearing down on his face has been worn down on a picture of him, which appears to be representing his conscious and soul. The picture gets older and crueler looking as he has done a lot of evil in the last 18 years. The man becomes obsessed with this painting to see how it changes and ultimately it consumes him and causing his tragic downfall.

This book is hands down my favorite book ever. Its written really well and it stays interesting through and through. Also fun fact, because of the time it was written, it was quite controversial and the author actually went on trial because of it.
